title: Visual analysis
description: The machine-readable half of the reference analysis, at examples/<project>/revisions/<id>/visual-analysis.json. It carries the parts later stages have to address by name — the named regions, the relational geometry, the anchor relationships, the shape-ownership cases and the open questions. visual-analysis.md keeps the prose observations. Per skills/workflows/create-template/SKILL.md the analysis describes the page in RATIOS and DEPENDENCIES, not pixels, and it must not pick GraphCompose primitives — that is the Architecture Mapper's job.

schemaVersion.description: On-disk contract version for this artifact.

provenance.description: Which reference, in which project, in which workspace, this analysis was written for. STAMPED BY THE TOOL, never by the author: scripts/write-artifact.mjs computes it from disk when the artifact becomes canonical and replaces whatever the document arrived with, and scripts/check-analysis.mjs recomputes and compares. A value the author writes is a value a copying agent copies, and copying is exactly what this catches — a run once imported another project's revision folder wholesale, landing a byte-identical visual-analysis.json, and the barrier passed because validating says the document is well-shaped, not that anybody looked at this reference. All three parts are bound because in that incident the two projects shared an id AND the same reference bytes; only the workspace differed. Revision is deliberately absent: pass.mjs carries a parent's sources forward, which is the loop working.

project.description: Project id the analysis was written for.

workspace.description: Digest of the workspace root the project lives in. Hashed rather than stored because the absolute path is the user's directory layout and belongs in nobody's committed artifact.

sha256.description: One digest over every reference page, each page's filename folded in with its bytes so that renaming or reordering pages is a different fingerprint.

pages.description: The reference page files hashed, in page order. source.png is excluded — re-importing the same page from a different source file is not a different reference.

bytes.description: Total size of the hashed pages, for a reader comparing two fingerprints by eye.

page.description: The page the document is built on. This used to be one free-text field holding "A4", which is what gets written when nothing measures: three projects on disk were built at A4 from references that were not A4 (mocha-profile-cv 9.5% out, cv-reference 4.9%, navy-executive-cv 4.2%), and every gate passed, because visual-diff --scale-reference resamples the reference to the render's exact width AND height and so stretches a wrong page size away immediately before the pixels are compared. The size is now measured by scripts/import-reference.mjs at import and recorded in template-project.json as referenceGeometry; this block carries it forward with the evidence attached, so a later reader can tell a measurement from an assumption.

format.description: The GraphCompose page constant this maps to — "A4", "LETTER", "LEGAL" — or "CUSTOM" when the page is DocumentPageSize.of(w, h). Note that aspect alone cannot tell A4 from A3 from A5: they share 1:root-2 by construction, so a reference measured as "A4" may be an A3 poster, and the content decides that.

orientation.description: Taken from the measurement, not from the look of the document. A landscape page is still its constant, turned: DocumentPageSize.A4.landscape().

referencePx.description: The reference image's own pixel dimensions, copied from the import's measurement. This is the evidence: it is what makes `aspect` checkable by someone who was not there, and it is the field whose absence let the page size be assumed for as long as it was.

aspect.description: height / width of the reference, as measured. Must agree with referencePx.

sizePt.description: The page the template actually builds at, in PDF points, as it will be passed to DocumentPageSize. Stated in points rather than left implicit in `format` because a CUSTOM page has no constant to name, and because a reader comparing this with referencePx can see for themselves how far the built page is from the measured one.

sizeSource.description: How the page size was arrived at. measured-standard: the reference matched a standard within tolerance and nobody had to be asked — import-reference exits 0 and says which. user-confirmed-standard / user-confirmed-custom: the reference matched nothing (import-reference exits 5 with the question), the user was asked, and this is their answer. There is deliberately no fourth value for "chose a size without measuring or asking": that is the defect this field exists to make impossible to record silently.

sizeDecision.description: What the user was asked and what they answered, in one or two sentences. Required whenever sizeSource is a user-confirmed value: the choice between a nearby standard and the exact measured size is not recoverable from the numbers afterwards — both are defensible — so the reason is recorded at the moment it is known.

margins.description: Margins expressed relationally where possible, e.g. "~7% of page width". Descriptive, not decided on. One sentence or several: the corpus writes both, and `render-artifact-md` renders a string and a list identically, so pinning one serialisation refused a run for a choice nothing downstream could tell apart.

regions.description: Named regions of the reference, in reading order. Every later artifact addresses regions by these ids: architecture-plan.json maps region -> render method, and visual-review.json reports mismatches per region.

contains.description: Elements inside the region, named the way a reader would name them. Descriptive, not decided on. One sentence or several: the corpus writes both, and `render-artifact-md` renders a string and a list identically, so pinning one serialisation refused a run for a choice nothing downstream could tell apart.

proportions.description: The region's share of its parent, as a ratio or weight — never a pixel width. E.g. "0.31 of the content row".

notes.description: Descriptive, not decided on. One sentence or several: the corpus writes both, and `render-artifact-md` renders a string and a list identically, so pinning one serialisation refused a run for a choice nothing downstream could tell apart. Null is an explicit "nothing to add".

bounds.description: The region as FRACTIONS of the page, top-left origin. Optional but cheap — four numbers — and it is what makes the region croppable: crop-region projects one fractional rect onto the reference and the render, whatever their resolutions, so a correction pass reads two small crops instead of two full pages. A region without bounds cannot be cropped, and the tool refuses rather than guessing.

role.description: What the region IS to the page, not what it contains. Required: a region with no role states no contract for how it may be built, and check-region-primitives cannot check it. page-header / page-footer are chrome that repeats on every page and must map to DocumentSession.header/.footer (or the version equivalent), never be drawn as body content and never bleedToEdge, which extends a fill past the margin to the paper edge. table-header repeats at the top of every page its table reaches (TableBuilder.repeatHeader). table must be built with addTable, not as rows of shapes. image must use addImage and icon addSvgIcon — a filled rectangle or a coloured disc standing in for either matches the box and nothing inside it. background is page-level fill behind everything; panel, divider and content carry no build contract.

layoutProportions.description: The page described in ratios and dependencies. Base constants derived from these land in architecture-plan.json.

anchors.description: Every element whose placement depends on another element, stated as a relationship rather than an offset. The Architecture Mapper turns each into a named engine primitive (LayerAlign, TextAlign, weights(...), ...).

relationship.description: E.g. "centred on", "pinned to the top-right of", "baseline-aligned with".

region.description: Region id this anchor belongs to.

shapeOwnership.description: Every container that owns content: initials or icons inside circles, labels inside bordered boxes, content inside cards, images clipped by shapes, badges anchored on a boundary. One entry per DISTINCT container — ten competency boxes built alike are one entry with repeats: 10, not ten entries. Each entry MEASURES the container rather than naming a style of it. This used to be three prose strings, and a run described a rounded rectangle of radius ~3px on a 32px box as a "rounded capsule shape with subtle border"; the mapper carried the word forward and the author implemented cornerRadius(15), a capsule. Nothing was lying: the schema had nowhere to put a radius, and the guidance offered the taxonomy "circles / pills or badges / rounded cards", which has no bucket for a rectangle with a small radius. Ratios throughout, never pixels, so the numbers survive any resolution.

relationship.description: What the ownership MEANS where geometry cannot say it — "the ring is the marker itself, page fill inside, so the rail is hidden where it crosses". Not the place for shape adjectives: those are measured below.

region.description: Region id this container sits in.

bounds.description: The container as FRACTIONS of the page, top-left origin — the same frame regions use. For a repeated container this is the FIRST instance. Required, because it is what turns every other field here from a claim into a checkable one: check-analysis samples the reference inside these bounds and just outside them, and refuses a fill.present that the pixels contradict. A run measured this container's shape, radius, sizing and repeat count correctly and got fill.present wrong, and the wrong answer was the defect a reader saw first.

repeats.description: How many identical instances of this container the reference shows. Repeated components are built once and driven by data; recording the count is what tells the author that.

shape.description: The outline. `pill` is reserved for a capsule whose radius really is half its height — it is NOT a synonym for "quite rounded". If the corners are rounded at all but not fully, this is `rounded-rectangle` and cornerRadiusRatio carries how much.

cornerRadiusRatio.description: Corner radius divided by the SHORTER side of the container. 0 is a square corner, 0.5 is a capsule or a circle. This is the field that makes rectangle-versus-pill a measurement instead of a word: the box that was called a capsule measures 0.09. A number sets all four corners. When they differ, name them — a panel with one rounded corner has no honest single value, and two models given the same such panel wrote 0 and 0.18 rather than saying so. Omitted corners in the object form are square. Required for every shape; use 0.5 for circle and ellipse.

sizing.description: How WIDE the container is. `fill-parent` spans its parent's content width, so a stack of them share both edges; `hug-content` shrinks to what is inside, so each one differs. Ten boxes with a common left AND right edge are fill-parent — the give-away is that the short label and the long one end at the same place. Getting this wrong is not subtle and has no other field to live in.

fill.description: The interior. A container that shows the page or panel behind it has fill.present = false — that is a different thing from a fill that happens to match the background, because the second one paints and the first one does not.

color.description: Hex, when there is a fill.

stroke.description: The border. A container defined ONLY by its border — no fill, the ground showing through — is common and was previously unrecordable; it is fill.present false with stroke.present true.

widthRatio.description: Stroke width divided by the container's shorter side. A hairline on a 32px box is about 0.03.

padding.description: Space between the container's edge and its content, each side as a fraction of the container's SHORTER side. Asymmetry matters and averaging it away is how content ends up optically off-centre.

gap.description: Space BETWEEN the container's children, as a fraction of the container's shorter side. Distinct from padding: one is the frame, the other is the rhythm inside it.

contentAlign.description: Where the content sits inside the container. Both axes, because a box whose text is vertically centred and one whose text sits on the baseline differ visibly and the difference has no other home.

spacingToNext.description: Gap to the next instance of this container, as a fraction of the container's shorter side. Only meaningful when repeats > 1, and it is what makes a stack's rhythm reproducible.

notes.description: Anything the numbers above could not carry, including how coarse an estimate is.

icons.description: Icons whose size or placement is independent of the text beside them. An icon reduced to an inline glyph at the text's own size is one of the reconstruction errors this exists to stop: the reference's icons were roughly half again the cap height and vertically centred, and nothing recorded that, so they were emitted as text-sized inline runs. Omit icons that genuinely are inline glyphs at text size — say so with inline: true rather than leaving them out, if in doubt.

id.description: What this icon is, matching the asset request's token where there is one.

sizeRelativeToText.description: The icon's drawn height divided by the height of the text it sits beside. 1.0 is text-sized; 1.45 is half again as tall. The single number that stops an icon becoming a glyph.

boundsRatio.description: The icon's box as fractions of its region, when it is placed independently rather than in a text run.

verticalAlign.description: Against the text beside it. `baseline` and `center` differ by a visible amount at any icon larger than the text.

gapToText.description: Space between the icon and the text, as a fraction of the icon's height.

inline.description: true when the icon is part of the text run and flows with it; false when it is its own child, positioned independently. The two build differently and cannot be swapped.

roles.description: Which face each type role uses, and whether that was measured or assumed. The prose fields below describe the type; this one commits to it.

fontName.description: The FontName constant the template will use, e.g. "LATO".

size.description: Type size in points, from `typography.mjs search --role <name>`. The scale that search needs is page.referencePx.width / page.sizePt.width. Without this the size is chosen by trial against whether a line wraps, which trades the size away to avoid fixing the column: one run set its contacts to 6.2 then 6.4pt so the longest address would fit.

source.description: measured: a recorded `typography.mjs match` ranked this family near the top for this role. assumed: someone chose it and said why.

sample.description: The exact string the crop contains, so the match can be reproduced.

crop.description: The crop of the reference that was matched.

why.description: Required when source is "assumed": what makes this the right face when nothing measured it.

colors.description: Colour roles rather than a raw swatch list, so the theme tokens in architecture-plan.json have something to map to.

usedIn.description: Descriptive, not decided on. One sentence or several: the corpus writes both, and `render-artifact-md` renders a string and a list identically, so pinning one serialisation refused a run for a choice nothing downstream could tell apart.

iconifyCandidates.description: Iconify set/name candidates, e.g. "mdi:email-outline". Descriptive, not decided on. One sentence or several: the corpus writes both, and `render-artifact-md` renders a string and a list identically, so pinning one serialisation refused a run for a choice nothing downstream could tell apart.

imagesLogos.description: Descriptive, not decided on. One sentence or several: the corpus writes both, and `render-artifact-md` renders a string and a list identically, so pinning one serialisation refused a run for a choice nothing downstream could tell apart.

assets.description: What the Asset Resolver will have to fetch. The authoritative request is asset-request.json.

unclearParts.description: Where the reference could not be read with confidence. skills/workflows/create-template/SKILL.md forbids silently guessing, so an assumption recorded here is the contract for what was assumed.

notes.description: Prose the rest of this schema cannot carry — a table comparing revisions, a paragraph of causal reasoning — emitted verbatim by scripts/render-artifact-md.mjs under a Notes heading. Markdown blocks. This exists so the reading copy stays generated: narrative belongs here, not in a hand-written .md twin that can disagree with this file.

flow.description: The fixed-vs-flowing decision, made explicitly at analysis time. A one-page invoice SCREENSHOT is not a one-page DOCUMENT: the sample shows four line items, real data brings thirty, and a template built as a fixed page breaks on the first real dataset. Recording the decision here is what forces the question to be asked while the reference is in front of the analyst, not after the first overflow bug.

kind.description: fixed: the page IS the artifact (CV, certificate, poster) - content is curated to fit. flowing: content volume is data-driven (invoice line items, transactions, an article) and the layout must paginate.

drivenBy.description: For flowing documents: the region id whose content grows with real data, e.g. line-items.

overflowExpectation.description: One sentence of reasoning: why real data will or will not spill past the page the reference shows. This is the sentence that decides whether the example data must include enough rows to reach page 2.

pageEnumeration.description: Whether the reader has to be able to tell that a page is missing. It is not decoration and it is not for every document: an invoice, a statement, an estimate, a formal proposal or a report is a record someone may print, post or file, and a page that vanishes from it should be detectable. A CV or a poster does not carry that duty. Recording the decision structurally is what stops it being made by whether the analyst happened to notice a page number in the reference.

required.description: true when a missing page must be detectable from the page itself.

reason.description: One sentence: why this document does or does not carry that duty.

location.description: Which chrome zone carries it. Maps to DocumentSession.footer(...) / .header(...) with DocumentHeaderFooterZone.

format.description: The literal chrome text, with GraphCompose's placeholders, e.g. "Page {page} of {pages}". The {pages} half is the part that makes a missing page detectable; "Page 3" alone does not.

repeat.description: every-page is the default. after-first suppresses it on a cover page, via DocumentPageNumbering.showOnFirstPage(false).

then.description: A flowing document has more than one page in its future, so whether the reader can tell a page is missing is a decision someone has to make. Requiring the field forces it to be made rather than defaulted by omission; recording `required: false` with a reason is a perfectly good answer.
